canonical.title: WSL2 as rung zero — what it proves, and the exact wall it hits

parent.title: Testing the waters: a staged, reversible path from a Windows dev workstation to Linux

siblings.title: The staged ladder: what each rung of a Windows→Linux move actually proves
siblings.summary: A rung-by-rung ladder from WSL2 to full switch, with what each rung proves, what it structurally hides, the go/no-go signal, and the cost of retreating.

siblings.title: Dual-boot Linux next to Windows in 2026 without wrecking the Windows install
siblings.summary: Buy a second NVMe, keep the two OSes ignorant of each other, and pick Linux from the firmware boot menu — the layout with the smallest blast radius on your Windows install.

siblings.title: Dropbox on Linux and shared folders: what actually works in 2026
siblings.summary: The official Linux client now supports btrfs/zfs/xfs, but you cannot share one Dropbox folder between a Windows and a Linux install, and code repos do not belong in Dropbox at all.

siblings.title: Trial hardware and VM paths for evaluating Linux before you commit (2026)
siblings.summary: Live USB first (€10, 15 minutes, proves your actual hardware), then a full install on an external NVMe SSD (€90–150) — everything else is a detour.

siblings.title: Living in both OSes: running Windows and Linux for months without your setup rotting
siblings.summary: One source of truth per asset class, replicated by a tool that knows the OS difference — never a shared partition and never two hand-edited copies.

siblings.title: Exit criteria and the blocker inventory: decide the Linux switch on evidence, not vibes
siblings.summary: A fill-in blocker inventory plus tickable go/no-go criteria and a pre-committed rollback date for a Windows-to-Linux workstation trial.

sources.title: Comparing WSL Versions — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: WSL2 runs a Microsoft-built Linux kernel with full syscall compatibility and systemd, but performance across OS file systems is worse than WSL1; serial ports unsupported; kernel serviced by Windows Update.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel
sources.claim: The WSL2 kernel repo's current default branch is linux-msft-wsl-6.18.y.

sources.title: Advanced settings configuration in WSL — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Reference for .wslconfig and wsl.conf options: systemd boot flag, memory/processors, networkingMode values, autoMemoryReclaim default dropCache, sparseVhd, defaultVhdSize 1TB, hostAddressLoopback/ignoredPorts require mirrored mode, and the 8-second config-reload rule.

sources.title: File storage and performance across file systems — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Microsoft recommends against working across operating systems and says to store project files in the WSL (Linux) file system rather than /mnt/c.

sources.title: webbertakken/wsl-filesystem-benchmark
sources.claim: Measured filesystem throughput/IOPS for WSL native ext4 vs WSL to /mnt/c vs Windows to \\wsl$, showing 10-90% loss across the boundary.

sources.title: Systemd support is now available in WSL — Microsoft Command Line Blog
sources.claim: systemd support requires WSL 0.67.6+ and is enabled with [boot] systemd=true in /etc/wsl.conf followed by wsl.exe --shutdown.

sources.title: WSL Container is now available for public preview — Microsoft Command Line Blog
sources.claim: WSL Containers (wslc) entered public preview on 29 June 2026 as part of WSL 2.9.3, with GA targeted for autumn 2026.

sources.title: Debug .NET Core apps in WSL — Visual Studio docs
sources.claim: Visual Studio provides a WSL launch profile for debugging .NET apps on Linux without a separate VM or container.

sources.title: NVIDIA GPU Accelerated Computing on WSL 2
sources.claim: NVIDIA supports CUDA workloads inside WSL2 using the Windows host driver via GPU paravirtualization.

sources.title: CUDA on WSL2: how it works, how to set it up — cicoria.com
sources.claim: GPU access in WSL2 goes through /dev/dxg with stub libraries in /usr/lib/wsl/lib; installing a Linux GPU driver overrides the symlinks and breaks CUDA passthrough.

sources.title: microsoft/wslg
sources.claim: WSLg provides Wayland and X11 support via Weston with an RDP backend, PulseAudio audio, and GPU acceleration through Mesa's d3d12 Gallium driver, remoting individual application windows.

sources.title: Windows 11 WSL2 vs. bare metal Ubuntu benchmarks — Phoronix
sources.claim: Phoronix benchmarked Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 against bare-metal Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D with 32GB RAM and a PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSD, published 15 September 2025.

sources.title: Microsoft WSL2 on Windows 11 25H2: 10–20% overhead — WebProNews
sources.claim: WSL2 on Windows 11 25H2 shows roughly 10-15% CPU overhead and up to 20% on I/O versus bare-metal Ubuntu, reaching 85-95% of native performance in many tests.

sources.title: The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source — Windows Blogs
sources.claim: WSL was open sourced at Microsoft Build on 19 May 2025.

sources.title: WSL open source components — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Open-sourced WSL components are wsl.exe, wslservice.exe, the Linux init/gns/localhost daemons and the plan9 server; lxcore.sys, p9rdr.sys and p9np.dll remain closed.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL
sources.claim: The official WSL source repository on GitHub.

sources.title: DrvFs — wsl.dev technical documentation
sources.claim: Windows drives are exposed to WSL2 by a plan9 file server started by wslservice.exe; mount.drvfs can alternatively use virtio-plan9 or virtiofs depending on .wslconfig.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#4197 — filesystem performance much slower than WSL1 in /mnt
sources.claim: Long-standing open issue reporting WSL2 /mnt write throughput of 40.4 MB/s versus 442 MB/s under WSL1 on the same hardware.

sources.title: WSL2 per-device SWIOTLB pools for virtiofs — Box of Cables
sources.claim: virtiofs is enabled with virtiofs=true under [wsl2] and requires kernel 6.18.26.3-1 or newer; a PR merged 27 May 2026 gave each virtio device its own DMA pool, and plan9 remains the default.

sources.title: Hacker News: WSL2 faster Windows file access discussion
sources.claim: Hacker News discussion of WSL2's faster Windows file access reports a Hugo build at 50s on native WSL filesystem, 75s via virtiofs, versus an estimated 3-5 minutes on plan9.

sources.title: Solving painful syncing of node_modules with Dropbox — Medium
sources.claim: Dropbox and Google Drive cannot selectively ignore node_modules, making syncing of dependency trees extremely slow for repos inside synced folders.

sources.title: Running a full Ubuntu desktop on WSL2 with XRDP — wsl-ui.octasoft.co.uk
sources.claim: WSLg remotes individual windows rather than a whole desktop, so running a full DE requires XRDP; GNOME Shell needs 3D acceleration XRDP cannot provide and KDE Plasma 6.8 is Wayland-only.

sources.title: Full desktop shell in WSL2 using WSLg (XWayland) — GitHub gist
sources.claim: Running a full desktop shell inside WSL2 requires a community workaround rather than a supported configuration.

sources.title: Fixing clock skew with WSL 2 — stuartleeks.com
sources.claim: WSL2 clock skew occurs because the WSL VM's clock is not updated when the Windows host resumes from sleep or hibernate; the fix is sudo hwclock -s or a Kernel-Power triggered scheduled task.

sources.title: Connect USB devices to WSL — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: USB device support in WSL2 is not native and requires the usbipd-win project, attaching devices by bus ID; while attached the device cannot be used by Windows.

sources.title: dorssel/usbipd-win
sources.claim: usbipd-win is the USB/IP implementation used to attach Windows USB devices to WSL2.

sources.title: Accessing network applications with WSL — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: WSL2 defaults to NAT with its own virtualized ethernet adapter and a changing IP, requiring netsh portproxy for LAN access; mirrored mode requires Windows 11 22H2+ and does not support the IPv6 localhost address ::1.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#13068 — mirrored networking falls back to NAT
sources.claim: Mirrored networking silently falls back to NAT on Windows builds that lack the required features.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#9026 — snapd does not work inside WSL
sources.claim: snapd does not work inside WSL, a limitation open for years.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#11857 — systemd >= 256 needs plain cgroup v2
sources.claim: systemd 256 and later require plain cgroup v2 support, which WSL's hybrid cgroup v1 hierarchy did not provide.

sources.title: Memory Reclaim in WSL 2 — Microsoft Command Line Blog
sources.claim: WSL2 memory grows because the Linux page cache balloons; Microsoft's example shows 2 GB attributed to the VM on Windows while Linux in-use memory is only 50 MB.

sources.title: How to fix WSL2 disk space bloat — ashn.dev
sources.claim: The WSL2 ext4.vhdx grows but never shrinks when files are deleted; reclaiming space needs fstrim plus Optimize-VHD, or sparse mode.

sources.title: Sparse VHD storage usage does not shrink — Microsoft Q&A
sources.claim: Once a WSL VHD is sparse, Optimize-VHD refuses to compact it, so manual compaction is no longer available.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#5424 — inotify does not work for mounted folders
sources.claim: inotify events do not fire for files on Windows-mounted paths in WSL2, breaking hot reload and file watchers; polling is the workaround.

sources.title: Adjust case sensitivity — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: NTFS drives mounted in WSL are case-insensitive by default (case=off) while ext4 is case-sensitive; mixed-case files become inaccessible to Windows applications and git core.ignorecase must be set to match.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL#40519 — isolate distro cgroups
sources.claim: WSL added per-distro cgroup isolation for systemd instances, with an IsolateDistroCgroup .wslconfig option defaulting to true.

sources.title: Microsoft makes WSL more stable with architecture tweak — Neowin
sources.claim: The redesigned WSL resource management relies entirely on cgroup v2, breaking legacy cgroup v1 workloads unless IsolateDistroCgroup is set to false.

sources.title: WSL2 vs dual boot for learning Linux — vecosys.com
sources.claim: The right moment to move from WSL2 to dual boot is when the frustration stops being about Linux commands and becomes about wanting Linux to be the whole experience; WSL2 mistakes are easier to unwind than dual-boot mistakes.
